exposure: epidural anesthesia in vaginal intended breech deliveries
no epidural anesthesia in vaginal intended breech deliveries
outcome: Fetal morbidity (measured with modified PREMODA score)
Rate of manual assistance during delivery
cohort: 2122 women at term with a singleton breech pregnancy from 37 + 0 weeks of pregnancy on and a birth weight of at least 2500 g at the obstetric department of University hospital Frankfurt from January 2007 to December 2018
finding: Epidural anesthesia during vaginal breech delivery was not associated with increased fetal morbidity but was associated with a higher cesarean delivery rate, a higher rate of manual assistance during delivery, and a longer duration of birth.
mod_finding: Epidural anesthesia during vaginal breech delivery was associated with a higher cesarean delivery rate, a higher rate of manual assistance during delivery, and a longer duration of birth.
